skill.name: sales-enablement
skill.description: Use when creating sales collateral, objection handling, battlecards, scripts, and handoff materials so the agent follows the marketingskills playbook instead of producing generic marketing advice.
whenToUse: The user asks for help creating sales collateral, objection handling, battlecards, scripts, and handoff materials
A marketing task needs product, audience, positioning, and channel context before execution
The agent should create a repeatable sales enablement workflow instead of a one-off generic answer
The work needs clear success metrics, deliverables, and next steps for a growth or GTM motion

keyConcepts.explanation: Check for product marketing context first: If .agents/product-marketing.md exists (or .claude/product-marketing.md, or the legacy product-marketing-context.md filename, in older setups), read it before asking questions. Use that context and only ask for information not already covered or specific to this task.
Core part of the sales enablement workflow; use it to keep the agent focused on concrete marketing inputs, decisions, and outputs instead of vague recommendations.
Involve reps in creation. Use their language, not marketing's. If reps rewrite your deck before sending it, you wrote the wrong deck. Test drafts with your top performers first.

Tailor to persona, deal stage, and use case. A deck for a CTO should look different from one for a VP of Sales. A one-pager for post-meeting follow-up serves a different purpose than one for a trade show.
Reps need information in 3 seconds, not 30. Use bold headers, short bullets, and visual hierarchy. If a rep can't find the answer mid-call, the doc has failed.
Every claim connects to revenue, efficiency, or risk reduction. Features mean nothing without the "so what." Replace "AI-powered analytics" with "cut reporting time by 80%."

apiReference.purpose: Install the sales-enablement skill from coreyhaines31/marketingskills.

gotchas: Do not create sales collateral without knowing the buyer stage, objection, proof point, and seller motion.
Battlecards should be factual and usable in conversation, not competitor hit pieces.
Read product-marketing context first when present; otherwise the agent may ask repeated setup questions or make weak positioning assumptions.
Do not ship generic best practices without tying recommendations to the product, audience, channel, and conversion goal.
Separate strategy from execution: clarify the campaign decision before drafting assets or implementation steps.
